# SE worker-storage cargo cap-ten native fixture

This is disposable test apparatus for one exact Factorio2.0.77, Space Exploration0.7.57, published4.7.20002 source-to-current candidate progression. It is not a migration admission, a reporter-save reconstruction, or a release result.

The fixture uses the same complete actor bytes for source, candidate, and both cold roles. Its data stage logs the sorted active-mod tuple and the seven typed `settings.startup[name].value` rows. It also logs the constructed worker technology without accepting the legacy five-pack construction: the candidate configuration callback must see and reject that real state before it queues any work.

`prerequisites.lua` is a reviewed literal 98-row prerequisite declaration rooted at `worker-robots-storage-3`, `se-space-science-lab`, and `se-material-science-pack-1`. Runtime only iterates the declaration for labelled fixture setup; it does not discover prerequisites, call recursive research, or treat those grants as cargo completions.

The actor creates the actual electric `se-space-science-lab`, records its native researching speed10, creates a fixture-owned bounded electric producer, fills the real lab inventory with the seven captured science packs, and temporarily records a documented force laboratory-speed stimulus. It records the pinned-API technology-price and laboratory-productivity context but does not change either. It never changes a lab prototype, target science unit, formula, time, effect, continuation level, progress, or bonus. Source events4–8 and candidate events9–10 must be engine events with `by_script=false`; each event must increase only the player worker-storage bonus by one while every other existing force remains unchanged. After ordinary source completion the fixture pauses and stages only the level-nine/tail queue on the next tick, rather than assuming an unbounded native queue. The product transfer must map source `worker-robots-storage-4` work to `mir-worker-storage-default-4` before candidate work; the actor records the raw canonical, private, and head rows separately from that logical paid frame. The level-eleven cap probe requires the naturally disabled private endpoint before it tries queue admission, then retains the unrelated tail current/queue and all seven science-unit observations unchanged. Each F200 science row is a normal-quality tool and records `count - 1 + durability / max_durability` through the pinned `LuaItemStack`/`LuaItemCommon` and `LuaItemPrototype.get_durability` APIs, so the saved frames retain fractional tool loss. The host `.42` partial is only a synthetic reader exercise: native evidence must supply actual tool-unit observations and independently justify any cost/rounding conclusion. Cold handling has only a local `on_load` flag and reads the closed endpoint without feeding, saving, granting research, or initializing persistent state.
